messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
People around you are stressed: Betty Kowalski. The mood is tense.

The Millfield General follow-up landed well — the facilities director replied within two days acknowledging receipt and noting the unemployment context observation as 'exactly the kind of systems thinking we need in this role,' which Denise read as a positive signal without over-interpreting it. The garage owner finally responded to the four-tick-old memo: a brief email saying he was 'interested in principle but not ready to commit capital in this environment' — which Denise correctly treated as a functional no and formally closed that path, freeing her attention entirely for the external search. She submitted a targeted application to a new last-mile logistics hub that had opened in the industrial corridor east of downtown, specifically framing her 24/7 multi-shift operations background as relevant to a high-throughput sorting facility. Grace Okafor replied to Denise's update with a thumbs-up and the note: 'they called two more people from my program this week.'
